messages:
maya: Heads-up — saw a spike in preemptible evictions from us-east-2 around 03:12. A bunch of small long-polling streaming requests got dropped; latency tail jumped for a few minutes. Anyone else?

ops-bot: k8s: node/node-spot-7 terminated (PreemptibleInstanceEviction) — affected pods: 12. Event window: 03:11:58 -> 03:12:21.

sandeep: I saw the same. Two things immediate: 1) our current cutover requeues the whole request which replays ~2s of generation and repeats KV warmups; 2) batch headroom on fallback pool was exhausted so some requests got soft-failed.

eli: Proposal: add a tiny per-request micro-checkpoint every N tokens (e.g., 32 tokens) that stores minimal KV pointers + last-offset in Redis. On eviction we can resume by swapping the stream to a short-lived resumable token rather than full requeue. Latency cost should be <50ms extra per checkpoint.

zoe: Nice. How do we avoid blowing up Redis with writes for high throughput bursts?

eli: Keep the key size tiny and use TTL ~60s. Also only checkpoint when request latency > X or when sequence length > Y. Default default-off for short responses.

maya: Operationally I want a fallback policy that prefers non-preemptible for tail-sensitive routes. Maybe route by annotation: route.headers:X-llm-slo=tail -> prefer on-demand pool. That buys us predictable latency and fewer checkpoints.

sandeep: Agreed. Also add a middle tier: mixed-capacity pool with small ratio (10%) of on-demand headroom reserved for tail cutovers. If preemptible drains, we first burst into mixed pool, then spill into on-demand if mixed is full. This lowers cost compared to keeping full on-demand capacity.

eli: For the stream cutover mechanics: on eviction we emit a small resumable token to the client via the streaming socket, something like: 

```
STREAM-RESUME: {"id":"r_abc123","kv_ptr":"k:svc:abc:ptr","offset":256}
```
Client reconnects and server calls resume(r_abc123) which rehydrates KV pointers and continues generation. We keep the token opaque and single-use.

zoe: What about model variants? Could we fall back to a quantized variant with faster warmup but slightly worse quality to avoid requeue cost?

maya: Yes — fallback policy should have graded options: (1) resumable resume on same model, (2) quick-quantized fallback, (3) route to on-demand. Make this configurable per route.

sandeep: One more: make the resumable token include tracing info and cost-budget hint so billing/accounting can attribute partial replays. We had headaches reconciling token-replays in billing last quarter.

ops-bot: rollout: config change applied to staging cluster at 03:45. Canary on us-east-1a for mixed-pool 10% headroom.

eli: I'll draft a minimal design doc with config examples and a safe-enough default (checkpoint=32 tokens, ttl=60s, mixed_headroom=10%). Will attach shortly.

zoe: For tests: we should simulate bursty evictions and measure end-to-end tail p99 and token replays per request. Add chaos monkey scenario for sequential evictions across AZs.

maya: Sounds good. Priority: prevent customer-visible tail spikes. Action items: eli write doc, sandeep add routing flag, zoe add chaos test, ops to monitor canary. I'll sync tomorrow after initial canary results. :thumbsup:
